_about: The dashboard To-Do feed: a short, layman-readable daily checklist of curation work (for Sam) and engineering/pre-curation work (for Fable, the Claude session), rendered by cpl_todos.js as the 📋 To-Do button on every tab. Refreshed at every Rule-8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff (this file is the handoff distilled for the dashboard). Check-off state lives in each viewer's browser (localStorage) and resets when _as_of changes. Keep it SHORT — ≤ ~12 items; done items are deleted, not checked.
_as_of: 2026-08-11 (end of day) · SkyBridge — Sierra AI now lives on My College.
_status: My College now opens with Sierra AI itself — not a link to it. You pick your college in that box, and it suggests questions built from your own numbers: your waiting credit, the credential your peers already give credit for that you don't, and how you're doing overall. Below it there's a new section showing who MAP has on file for your college, so you can keep it current. Two corrections Sam caught went in the same day: the page had been saying credit was 'written onto the transcript' when checking Transcribe in MAP is a record-keeping step — Admissions & Records still enters it in the college's own system, by hand. And the funding pools now use their real tab names. Next session picks up MAP links, so the page can hand you off to where the work actually happens.

items.text: Twenty-five pieces of real feedback on Sierra are waiting to be read, eleven of them thumbs-down, the oldest sitting since 1 July. Measured live today — the automated test rows are excluded, and only four rows have ever been marked addressed.

You asked whether hiding groups under ten students loses useful data. Measured: it hides 320 of 436 credentials but only about 5% of students and 5% of units. So the cost is not the totals — it is that three quarters of individual credentials cannot be named. Worth deciding whether a different technique would keep the names.

Sam spotted that Sierra still cannot see EACR. Wire the prescriptive layer into Supabase — it knows, per credential, which colleges could adopt it and the course each one already teaches. That turns 'you could adopt CompTIA A+' into 'adopt it against the course you already run'.

Student-contact worklist, about ten minutes total: five colleges have a suggested counselling address nobody could verify (the network blocks their websites from here) — each needs about ten seconds in a browser to confirm; then fourteen colleges with no contact in MAP have a suggested one ready to send to the MAP team.

Two things here need a person, not a session: four colleges publish no usable address at all for a credit question, and the fifty-two colleges that do have a CPL Assistant were never checked for a student contact. Sessions are blocked from opening college websites, so this needs a human or a differently-connected runner.

There is now a district picker. Choosing a district narrows the college list and shows that district's colleges with the credit each one has already articulated and is waiting to award. Listed alphabetically on purpose — it is a list of work, not a league table.

Two things to ask the MAP team for, in one conversation: a feed of the CPL requests students submit (the one section of My College that cannot be built without it), and a durable row id for the student extract — the one we rely on today is an Access autonumber that renumbers on re-import.

Wire EACR's prescriptive layer into Supabase. It knows the local course each college most likely already teaches for a credential, which turns 'adopt CompTIA A+' into 'adopt it against the CIS-25 you already run' — on both My College and Sierra. Sam's catch, now carried three sessions.

Sierra AI is now embedded at the top of My College — same assistant as the CPL Assistant tab, just mounted there too, so you never leave the page. Worth trying the suggested questions; they're built from the selected college's own figures.

New section: who MAP has on file for a college — primary contact, coordinator, counselor, articulation officer and more, with blanks named. Moreno Valley's primary contact is one address stored eleven times; the page de-duplicates it now, but MAP still holds it that way.
Next: embed MAP links so someone with a MAP sign-in can jump straight to adopting an exhibit, working student records, or updating contacts. Each has a section on the page already waiting for it.
Port the three mock sections not yet live: the funding breakdown by goal, the list of what the waiting credit actually consists of, and a resources section like the CPL Fact Sheet's.
